skill.name: linear-issues-read
skill.description: Read Linear issues through Bun-based CLI commands with filters and issue detail lookup.
skill.summary: Read-only Linear issue lookup for AI coding agents.
skill.author: Bind

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally uses a Linear API key and may read it from .env, so credential exposure is the main confirmed risk. Most Ruby backtick detections are Markdown formatting false positives, while several Bun command examples represent intended external command execution. No prompt injection or hidden malicious intent was found in the audited files.

remediation.suggestion: Use a dedicated least-privilege Linear token, avoid shared tokens, and document that issue data may appear in terminal output.
Prefer secure environment injection and require explicit user consent before reading <git-root>/.env.
Keep Bun commands fixed, quote user-supplied filters, and warn users before running scripts from untrusted worktrees.
Declare expected Linear API network access separately from Bun installation documentation.

content.user_title: Read Linear Issues from the CLI
content.value_statement: Linear issue context is hard to inspect when work spans projects and teams. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code read Linear issues through a CLI.
actual_capabilities: Lists Linear issues with filters for team, project, assignee, status, and limit.
Retrieves one Linear issue by issue key or UUID.
Can return command output in table or JSON format.
Resolves team, user, and label names case-insensitively.
Displays CLI output directly for user review.
limitations: Requires a valid LINEAR_API_KEY and Bun runtime.
Provides read-only issue listing and detail views, not edits or comments.
Depends on the referenced CLI scripts being installed at the expected path.
Terminal output can expose private issue data to the active session.

use_cases.title: Check assigned work
use_cases.description: List active Linear issues for one assignee and review their current status.

use_cases.title: Review a project queue
use_cases.description: Filter issues by project to inspect open work before planning or standup.

use_cases.title: Inspect issue context
use_cases.description: Fetch one issue by key or UUID before implementing a requested change.

prompt_templates.prompt: List Engineering Todo issues as JSON, then group results by assignee and identify items without owners.

output_examples.input: List Engineering issues with a limit of 10.
output_examples.output: A terminal table shows up to ten matching issues with identifiers, titles, status, assignee, and project when available.
The issue detail view shows the title, description, current status, assignee, project, and related metadata.

output_examples.input: Review Todo issues for a project and summarize ownership.
output_examples.output: A concise summary groups the listed issues by assignee and calls out issues that need ownership review.

best_practices: Use a dedicated Linear API key with the minimum access needed.
Prefer narrow filters before requesting JSON output or summaries.
Review terminal output before sharing issue data outside the workspace.
anti_patterns: Do not use a shared administrator API key for routine issue lookup.
Do not run the referenced CLI scripts from an untrusted working tree.
Do not paste private issue output into public channels or logs.

faq.question: Does this skill modify Linear issues?
faq.answer: No. It documents read-only list and get commands. It does not create, update, comment, or close issues.

faq.question: What credential is required?
faq.answer: It requires LINEAR_API_KEY in the environment or in a project .env file.

faq.question: Can it filter issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports filters for team, project, assignee, status, result limit, and JSON output.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. The commands need access to Linear through the configured SDK and API key.

faq.question: Can it return JSON output?
faq.answer: Yes. Both list and get commands document a JSON output option.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The marketplace report marks it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
